references.text: Parallel text describing the third row of precious stones (lodesh, shebo, and achlama) on the breastplate when it was actually made, in accordance with the instructions given in Exodus 28:19.
The complete description of all four rows of precious stones on the breastplate, where verse 19 constitutes the third row.
Ezekiel's description of the precious stones in Eden, which shares several of the same stones mentioned in the high priest's breastplate.
The foundation of the new Jerusalem is adorned with precious stones that resemble those on the high priest's breastplate, showing continuity in biblical symbolism.
The prophecy about the rebuilt Jerusalem with precious stones, pointing back to the breastplate's symbolism and forward to the new Jerusalem.
Revelation uses the list of the breastplate's stones as an image for the foundation of the new Jerusalem, linking the mediator of the old covenant to the new covenant.
